title: The Law of Karma and the Birth of Vidura
body:
The Law of Karma and the Birth of Vidura

The ancestral cosmos of Hastinapur was deeply governed by the unyielding laws of Karma, illustrated by the birth of Vidura. Sage Mandavya, who had acquired great spiritual strength through silent penance and the practice of truth, lived in a forest hermitage. One day, a band of robbers hid their booty in his ashram while the sage was immersed in deep yoga. The king's soldiers tracked the robbers, found the stolen goods, and arrested Mandavya along with the thieves, assuming him to be their accomplice.
The king sentenced them all to be impaled on spears. Mandavya remained on the stake, surviving through his yogic power and repeating sacred chants. When the king realized his mistake, he released the sage and begged for his forgiveness. Mandavya sought out Lord Dharma, the god of justice, and demanded: 'Why was I subjected to this terrible torture? What sin did I commit to deserve this impalement?'
Lord Dharma replied: 'As a child, you tortured birds and bees by piercing them with sharp blades of grass. Every action, no matter how small, inevitably produces its results.' Mandavya, outraged, cursed Lord Dharma: 'A punishment decreed for a childhood mistake committed in ignorance is far in excess of justice. For this injustice, you shall be born as a mortal in the material world, born of a low-caste servant-maid.'
This curse was fulfilled when Vichitravirya died without children. To preserve the Kuru lineage, Satyavati summoned her son, Sage Vyasa, to perform Niyoga on the widowed queens Ambika and Ambalika. Ambika, frightened by Vyasa's austere, terrifying appearance, closed her eyes during their union, leading to her son Dhritarashtra being born blind. Ambalika turned pale with fear, leading to her son Pandu being born pale and sickly.
When Satyavati asked Vyasa to perform Niyoga once more, Ambika secretly sent her humble, devoted servant-maid in her place. The servant-maid received Vyasa with deep reverence and joy. From this union was born Vidura, the incarnation of Lord Dharma himself, who possessed unmatched wisdom, virtue, and scriptural knowledge, and served as the wise counsellor of Hastinapur.
